sections.html:
Eastpointe is a small, dense Macomb County city of 5.16 square miles. Most of what sellers deal with is rental registration, tax billing and school boundaries rather than a pre-sale inspection. Owners live in about seven of every ten homes, so many buyers are families looking for a first or second home.

The city peaked at 45,920 residents in 1970, slipped to 32,442 by 2010 and has hovered near 34,000 since. Downtown Detroit is ten miles southwest, and 8 Mile Road forms the southern edge of the city.

Rents are high against modest home values, so rented houses are common here and the city's rental registration rules come up in many sales.

The Building Department manages registration and inspection of every non-owner-occupied residential property, and tenants cannot occupy a rental until the city certifies it. If your house is rented, the buyer inherits that regime.

  • Rentals must be registered and inspected every two years from the application date.
  • If a property is certified at the time of sale, the certificate may transfer to the new owner when that owner registers within 14 days of purchase.
  • Owners and property managers complete a one-time registration separate from the property registration.
  • An owner who lives 50 miles or more from city hall must name a local agent.
  • A furnace or boiler must pass an inspection by a qualified contractor.

Vacant buildings have their own rule: register inside 45 days of the vacancy, renew each year until the property is occupied again, and obtain a certificate of compliance for re-occupancy. Call the Building Department at 586-445-3661 for rentals (extension 2269) or vacant properties (extension 2214).

Eastpointe Community Schools reaches most parcels. South Lake Schools claims the southeastern corner, and its Koepsell Elementary stands inside Eastpointe's borders. Confirm the district for your parcel before listing, since boundaries shape what a family will pay.

Gratiot Avenue (M-3) runs through the city, with I-94 and I-696 close by, and 8 Mile Road (M-102) and 9 Mile Road carry cross-town traffic. Commuters like that access, and it is worth mentioning in a listing.

The City Treasurer collects for the city, Macomb County, Macomb Community College, the intermediate school district, the state education tax and both school districts. About 30,000 bills go out each year, and both school districts ask that 100 percent of school tax appear on the summer bill.

  • Summer taxes are due July 1 with a September 1 deadline. Pay it all by September 1, or pay half by then and the other half by December 1.
  • Winter taxes are due December 1 with a February 15 deadline.
  • A summer balance left after September 1 grows by 1 percent a month, with 2 percent more from February 16.
  • A winter balance left after February 15 carries a 3 percent charge.
  • From March 1, unpaid taxes go to the Macomb County Treasurer at One South Main Street in Mount Clemens, with added penalties.

Eligible owners can defer summer taxes to February 15 if household income is $40,000 or less and they are 62 or older, disabled, a qualifying veteran, a surviving spouse or blind. The deferment application is due by September 15. For a payoff figure, call the taxes line at 586-445-3661, option 6.

The buyer signs the principal residence exemption form at closing if the house will be owner-occupied. The seller signs a request to rescind the exemption and files it with the assessor, which clears the seller's name from the homestead and lets the seller claim it on the next home.

Buyers owe the assessor a Property Transfer Affidavit, due 45 days after the transfer. Each late day costs $5, capped at $200. The taxable value is uncapped the year after a transfer, so the new owner's bill rises to match the assessed value, which the city sets at half of market value.

An owner who thinks the value is too high must appear in March, since that is the only month the Board of Review hears opinions of value. The July and December sessions deal with clerical errors, mutual mistakes of fact and hardship requests. A homeowner who loses can take the case to the Michigan Tax Tribunal by June 30.

On an Eastpointe sale the seller pays the state transfer tax, $3.75 on each $500 block of value (MCL 207.525). Macomb County adds a levy of its own under MCL 207.504. The county deed office at 586-469-7953 can tell you the current total, and the county treasurer collects it, with a 15-day deadline that starts when the deed is delivered.

MCL 207.526 exempts, among others, a deed that does nothing but straighten a boundary line and a land contract that has not yet passed legal title. A land contract buyer can still claim the principal residence exemption if the contract is recorded or recordable.

sections.h2: What a seller should do first
sections.html: Start by finding out whether the house is owner-occupied or rented. If it is rented, call the Building Department and ask whether the rental certificate is current and whether it can pass to a buyer who registers inside the 14-day window. Then call the taxes line for a payoff figure, and confirm which school district serves the parcel. With those three answers you can list the house, or talk to a cash buyer, knowing what the buyer will inherit and what the closing agent has to pay from your proceeds.

sections.h2: What a buyer will ask you for
sections.html: Expect a buyer's agent or lender to ask for the rental certificate if the house is a tenant-occupied property, proof that any vacant-building registration is current, and a clear tax payoff. Owner-occupant buyers will also want to know which school district serves the house. Have these papers ready before showings begin, and the offers you get will be based on facts instead of guesses. If a payoff shows a balance after March 1, the Macomb County Treasurer holds it, so allow time for that office to answer before your closing date.

faqs.q: Is there a pre-sale inspection for an Eastpointe house?
faqs.a: The city's rules cover rental registration and vacant property registration, not a general pre-sale inspection. If the house is a rental, the certificate may pass to the buyer if the buyer registers within 14 days. Call the Building Department to confirm your property's status.

faqs.q: When are Eastpointe summer and winter taxes due?
faqs.a: Summer bills are issued July 1 with a September 1 deadline, and winter bills December 1 with a February 15 deadline. Whatever is unpaid on March 1 goes to the Macomb County Treasurer.

faqs.q: How do I remove my principal residence exemption after selling?
faqs.a: Sign a request to rescind the exemption and file it with the Eastpointe Assessing Department. That clears your name from the homestead so you can claim the exemption on your next home.

faqs.q: What does the buyer file after an Eastpointe closing?
faqs.a: A Property Transfer Affidavit, filed at the Assessor's Office. The closing agent usually supplies the form, but the buyer must file it, and a filing later than 45 days costs $5 per day up to $200.

faqs.q: Which district serves an Eastpointe address?
faqs.a: Eastpointe Community Schools covers most parcels, while the southeastern corner belongs to South Lake Schools. Look up your parcel before you list.
